newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Wharf expected to refinance.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Wharf expected to refinance.

text.p: Wharf Holdings) Ltd is expected to join a long line of blue chips taking advantage of low rates to refinance, bankers said on Wednesday.
They said Chase Manhattan Asia, Standard Chartered Investment Banking and Hang Seng Bank Ltd were arranging the HK$3.0 billion loan.

They could not give details of pricing for the deal, which was expected to be launched in the afternoon, although one banker close to the deal said the margin would be 46 basis points over the Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate.
Bankers said Wharf was the latest of a string of Hong Kong blue chips to refinance recently, taking advantage of funding costs which have fallen at least 20 basis points this year.
Wharf last year raised HK$5.2 billion (increased from HK$3 billion) through a five-year facility paying a margin of 55 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR).

Blue chips recently raising funds to wholly or partly refinance include CITIC Pacific Ltd, seeking HK$8 billion, Hutchison Whampoa Ltd (HK$10 billion), and Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd (HK$10.5 billion).
Banks have also been raising cash both take advantage of lower rates and to lend to corporates as they refinance.
Rizal Commercial Banking Corp is seeking to raise US$75 million in a two-tranche deal, bankers said.
They said tranche A was for US$25 million and three years and paid a coupon of 70 basis points over the six-month LIBOR.
The US$50 million offered in Tranche B was for five years, and paid 85 basis points over six-month LIBOR, bankers said.
Issue price was par, and arrangers are Sanwa International Finance and Standard Chartered Bank.
Fees are 21 basis points for co-arrangers committing US$3 million to Tranche A, and 40 basis points for co-arrangers committing US$6 million to Tranche B.
Some bankers criticised the 77 basis points all-in for tranche A at the top level, saying it was too aggressive.
Bankers said Allied Banking Corp, which has a higher rating than Rizal, paid an all-in of 82 basis points last month in a three-year issue, five basis points more than Rizal.
Rizal's fees are 15 basis points for co-lead managers committing US$2 million to Tranche A, or 30 basis points for US$4 million to Tranche B.
Its fees are nine basis points for managers committing US$1 million to Tranche A, and 25 basis points for US$2 million for Tranche B.
Issue proceeds are for general funding purposes, bankers said
